title: Comprehensive Experimental Ablation Study & Multimodal Framework Evaluation
scope: Dynamic Multimodal Financial Risk Assessment Using Financial Indicators and Financial News
research_option: Option B: Research-Ready Financial + News Risk-Scoring Framework

experiments.architecture: XGBoost Classifier (83 features, with lagged distress x81)
experiments.notes: Includes previous-period distress state (x81); evaluated at validation-optimized threshold 0.40.

experiments.architecture: XGBoost Classifier (82 features, NO lagged target x81)
experiments.notes: Relies purely on structural financial ratios; higher PR-AUC (0.3764 vs 0.3236) and lower Brier calibration score (0.0255).

experiments.architecture: 2-Layer PyTorch LSTM (90-day FinBERT sentiment sequences, 6 features)
experiments.evaluation_population: S&P 500 Historical News Sequences (Held-out T >= 2022, 10,821 samples)
experiments.notes: Evaluated on forward 30-day corporate risk events (AUC 0.5435). Serves as an auxiliary sentiment forecasting component; not evaluated as a financial distress classifier.

experiments.architecture: XGBoost Financial + FinBERT Current Sentiment (Static Risk Concatenation)
experiments.notes: Combines spot financial distress probability with instant headline sentiment risk score.

experiments.architecture: Fixed Baseline Fusion: 0.60 * Financial Risk + 0.40 * News Risk
experiments.notes: Fixed weight baseline combining structural financial distress with 90-day LSTM sequence risk.

experiments.architecture: Rule-Based Coverage-Adaptive Fusion (Dynamic alpha volume & volatility weighting)
experiments.notes: Rule-based coverage-adaptive heuristic dynamically reallocating weights based on reporting volume alpha and sentiment volatility. Not a learned neural model.

scientific_conclusions: Financial Model Autonomy: Removing lagged feature x81 preserves an outstanding ROC-AUC of 0.9232 and increases PR-AUC to 0.3764 (with lower Brier score 0.0255 vs 0.0262), proving that underlying financial ratios drive prediction rather than target auto-correlation.

Threshold Optimization Efficacy: Validation-based threshold tuning (0.40-0.45) increases distressed-class recall from 35.48% (at default 0.50 threshold) to 48.39% with x81, and to 38.71% without x81 on held-out test data (Time 11-14).

Textual Sentiment Role: Standalone news sequence LSTM achieves ROC-AUC 0.5435 on forward 30-day sentiment shocks, confirming that corporate news flows exhibit high noise and modest standalone predictability. It is evaluated as an auxiliary sentiment forecasting component, not as a standalone predictor of balance-sheet distress.

Multimodal Risk-Scoring Framework: In the absence of a common ground-truth target across the disjoint datasets, the multimodal framework operates as an adaptive decision-support system. It combines structural accounting distress probabilities with real-time news volatility without fabricating spurious cross-dataset entity joins.
